CDCAtlas working guidance

Source: AGENTS.md

Adapted from the usethis::use_tidy_agents() template committed in PR #39. Do not regenerate this file in place; preserve the project-specific guidance and review changes against the committed version.

Scope and authority

This file applies to all substantive CDCAtlas work: implementation, design, debugging, tests, documentation and review. Read REVIEWING.md for shared review standards. More specific subdirectory guidance also applies to implementation. Neither repository files nor skills expand the user’s permissions; direct user instructions control.

Repository: https://github.com/VagishHemmige/CDCAtlas Documentation: https://vagishhemmige.github.io/CDCAtlas/ The default branch was verified as master on 2026-11-13; verify it again when selecting a base. This guidance does not cover CDCLocator or other repos.

Use available project conversations to understand intent. Automated runs may not receive every conversation or uploaded file. State material context gaps. Record agreed technical decisions and rationale in existing issues and design records, linking them from PRs and relevant documentation. Available project pages can provide context; do not assume every assistant can access them. Preserve the durable technical decision without copying private conversations. A new repository notes directory is not implied. Distinguish accepted decisions from proposals in issue discussions.

Architecture and existing rationale

CDCAtlas is a development-stage R client for selected reverse-engineered AtlasPlus endpoints, with a separate modeled-estimation pipeline:

  • R/get_atlas.R, R/validate_input.R, R/build_payload.R: validate requests and construct payloads; county requests are split by state.
  • R/internal-request.R: HTTP transport, response decoding, labels, rate limiting and caching. R/sysdata.rda supplies internal lookup data.
  • R/impute_suppressed.R: existing assumption-based county estimates.
  • R/no_county_cases.R: state totals minus supplied county counts.
  • R/extrapolate_from_county.R: ACS denominators and allocation to tracts or block groups; R/atlas-pipeline.R supplies shared keys and checks.
  • tests/testthat/: synthetic tests and separately gated live checks.
  • vignettes/articles/getting-started.Rmd and vignettes/articles/extrapolation.Rmd: website articles (not built with the package) on usage, assumptions and limitations; docs/ contains generated site output.

Read the relevant source and documentation before advising or changing it. Issue #29 records the pipeline design, but some proposed names and arguments differ from the implemented API. #23 discusses validation layers; #27 and #30 record suppression/remainder and geography concerns. Recheck their current discussion and implementation rather than treating every proposal as adopted policy. #45 proposes a source interpretation article; do not claim it exists until it is committed. #4 tracks the currently uncommitted data-generation scripts. Do not invent their contents.

Implementation and approval

A review or explanation request alone does not authorize implementation. For requested changes, draft and self-review in an isolated workspace. The user’s connected working copy, synced reference files (including sources/) and active RStudio session remain read-only: no execution there.

Before commitment, obtain the user’s approval for each behavior-changing file, including definitions, arguments, outputs, request payloads, missingness and derived estimates. Finish the concrete draft and appropriate checks first. Show a readable diff for every changed file: side-by-side when supported, otherwise unified. Show complete new files and provide access to complete changed files. Explain what changed, why, behavior changes and validation actually performed. Separate human-written and mechanical generated changes. Request approval for the specific files and revision shown; a summary alone is insufficient. Compare consequential alternatives with meaningful synthetic examples when feasible. When two or more alternatives are reasonable, present them with their tradeoffs and a recommendation before settling the design. Consider a function argument with a recommended default when alternatives serve plausible user needs; an argument is a proposal, not an automatic requirement. Seek the maintainer’s decision before implementation. Do not conceal unresolved scientific definitions or present an invalid method as an equally acceptable choice. Use meaningful synthetic comparisons where feasible.

What each assistant may commit, push, post, merge or delete is set by the maintainer outside this repository. This file grants none of those permissions. Inspect mechanical generated changes before including them with approved source; material behavior changes after approval require renewed approval. Self-review is not independent review. Identify assistant authorship in the PR body so independent review can be routed correctly.

Data and execution boundaries

Never access, copy, upload or expose restricted or patient-level data. For uncertain provenance, identify only the path and request verification without reproducing values. Public aggregate CDC data may be retrieved for relevant checks. Do not attempt to reconstruct suppressed values or identify individuals. Existing imputation code is not permission to recover hidden counts: inspect it or test its mechanics with synthetic data, and keep modeled estimates explicitly distinct from observed surveillance values. Distinguish statistical estimation under explicit assumptions and uncertainty from recovering hidden observed counts. A censored model or calibration method is not automatically prohibited, nor automatically validated or authorized. Assess its purpose and data flow against the user’s permissions before using live data. Do not use residuals or auxiliary tables to recover CDC-suppressed values; synthetic checks remain available for evaluating method mechanics.

Use small, obviously synthetic unit fixtures. Inspect startup files, helpers, test configuration and package load-time behavior before execution; do not load secrets or copy private startup settings. Use isolated temporary/cache locations and clean sessions. Do not edit or regenerate data/ without explicit approval. Propose data-raw/ changes and explain intended regeneration for approval; changes to generated R/sysdata.rda likewise require explicit approval and known provenance.

New package code writes only to tempdir() unless the caller explicitly supplies a destination. Existing R/internal-request.R uses memoise::cache_filesystem(tools::R_user_dir("CDCAtlas", "cache")). This is an existing convention, not authorization to extend it. Inspect cache creation, persistence and freshness before proposing changes (#14); isolate existing writes during checks. Changing that behavior requires approval.

CI has a CENSUS_API_KEY repository secret for the live tests and the site build. Workflows read it with ${{ secrets.CENSUS_API_KEY }}; never print, log or commit its value.

Run devtools::document() only in isolation when relevant; exclude unrelated Rd and incidental DESCRIPTION/RoxygenNote churn. Do not run formatters unless requested. Inspect generated exports/imports rather than assuming they are safe.

Skills and validation

Use applicable R package-development and critical-code-review guidance for substantive work. Add testing and test-review guidance for tests or untested behavior, cli guidance for conditions, CRAN guidance for DESCRIPTION/examples/ vignettes or CRAN preparation, and lifecycle guidance for deprecations. Use style guidance for requested style reviews. Names vary by environment: r-testthat / testing-r-packages, r-cli / cli, r-cran-extrachecks / cran-extrachecks, and r-lifecycle / lifecycle. Use the installed equivalent.

Disclose unavailable skills or references. Permission boundaries and this project’s no-unsolicited-formatting rule take precedence over skill defaults.

Prefer regression tests demonstrating the bug before the fix. Keep routine tests reproducible and independent of live services. Run targeted public API checks separately when useful and permitted; mocks establish code behavior, not current service compatibility. Report actual runtime and network availability rather than assuming either.

Separate source inspection, personally executed synthetic checks, recorded responses, live API checks, observed CI and author-reported validation. Record live retrieval dates, tested requests and coverage gaps without keys or credentials. Supply exact commands for remaining maintainer checks and vignette rebuilding when relevant, with prerequisites and side effects. The established pipeline-validation workflow includes the full live suite with CDCATLAS_LIVE_TESTS=true and devtools::test(filter = "live"). Before using that workflow, inspect all selected tests, including imputation, and their data/cache effects. Run the full suite only when every selected path is permitted; otherwise run the permitted subset and report the coverage gap. A test flag is not authorization to cross the user’s data boundaries.

Automation triggers, comment permissions, own-PR exclusions, deduplication and notifications belong in automation configuration. This file does not start automation or grant publishing authority. Each assistant’s automation status is maintained outside these shared technical standards.

Package conventions retained from the template

  • Use US English and sentence-case headings. Follow existing tidyverse style, using the base pipe and single-line anonymous-function shorthand where appropriate. Do not perform unrelated style cleanup.
  • Put tests for R/{name}.R in tests/testthat/test-{name}.R, near related tests. Keep test code inside test_that(); shared setup belongs in helpers. Use meaningful tests for new behavior and specific expectations with useful failures. For errors/warnings, prefer snapshots when message text matters; use class-based expectations when testing a known condition class. Avoid .package mocking of another package’s namespace; use a local service boundary that can be mocked.
  • Document and export public functions with roxygen2. Internal documentation should not create public help topics; use @noRd when appropriate. Wrap roxygen comments to 80 characters. Add new public topics to _pkgdown.yml and check reference coverage with pkgdown::check_pkgdown(). Redocument relevant roxygen changes in isolation.
  • Give user-facing changes a NEWS.md bullet, except small documentation changes, internal refactoring and fixes introduced in the current development version. Put the function name early; mention the related issue in parentheses. Keep each bullet on one line, order function bullets alphabetically, and put non-function bullets first. Credit a GitHub username only when the PR contributor is not already a package author.
  • When committing is authorized, use Markdown in the commit message without wrapping its lines; include Fixes #num. on its own line when applicable.

Documentation maintenance and publication

The paths above describe the current layout. Update them when the cleanup in #20 and #43 lands. Air adoption in #42 does not itself authorize unsolicited formatting.

.Rbuildignore excludes AGENTS.md and REVIEWING.md from package builds, not from pkgdown. Both root Markdown files can become unlinked website pages, including search and sitemap entries. #40 currently defers the publication fix. Do not claim these files are unpublished or private. A publishing change requires a separately reviewed build/deployment solution; search exclusion alone does not remove the pages.
